chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
If you perform the funeral prayer over an enemy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then say: O Allah, we know of him only that he was an enemy to You and to Your Messenger.

O Allah, fill his grave with fire, and fill his interior with fire, and hasten him to the Fire, for he used to be loyal to Your enemies, show enmity to Your friends, and hate the Ahl al-Bayt of Your Prophet. O Allah, constrict his grave upon him.
Then when he is lifted, say: O Allah, do not raise him and do not purify him.
And if he was mustaḍʿaf, then say: O Allah, forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.
So if you do not know what his condition was, then say: O Allah, if he loved goodness and its people, then forgive him, have mercy on him, and pardon him.
And if the mustaḍʿaf had some connection to you, then seek forgiveness for him by way of intercession from you, not by way of wilayah.

key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِ نَبِيِّكَ: the family of Your Prophet; the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَكَ: Your friends or allies; those devoted to Allah
key_terms.عَدُوِّ ٱللَّهِ: an enemy of Allah; one characterized here by opposition to Allah, His Messenger, and His awliyāʾ
key_terms.قَبْرَهُ: his grave; the place associated here with post-death punishment or constriction
key_terms.مُسْتَضْعَفًا: a weakened or excused person lacking full clarity or capacity in religious understanding
key_terms.ٱلشَّفَاعَةِ: intercession; seeking forgiveness on someone's behalf

ai.seo_question: What should be said in the funeral prayer for an enemy of Allah, a mustaḍʿaf, or someone of unknown condition?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines different supplications to be recited in salat al-janazah depending on the deceased person's religious condition: an open enemy of Allah and the Ahl al-Bayt, a mustaḍʿaf, or someone whose state is unknown. It reflects distinctions in loyalty, enmity, intercession, and accountability in the afterlife within the funeral prayer context.
